model_note.S:
CC: My right knee has been sore and swollen since I twisted it.

HPI: 54-year-old male. Right knee pain for 3 days. Twisting injury on a planted foot while carrying a box; no fall. Medial right knee pain. No radiation. Aching with catching pain during rotation. Weight bearing with limp; pain 6/10. Delayed swelling over the first evening. Catching without true locking or giving way. Worse with twisting, stairs and deep flexion. Relief with rest, protected ice and elevation. Acetaminophen 650 mg twice yesterday. Prior activity-related ache and brief morning stiffness.

PMH: Hypertension; crystal-confirmed gout episode last year.

PSH: Hernia repair at 30; no knee surgery.

Meds: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; no urate-lowering therapy.

SH: Former smoker: 5 pack-years, quit 15 years ago. Approximately six beers weekly. No recreational drugs. Grocery stocker; frequent lifting and squatting. Lives with wife; one flight of home stairs.

FH: Mother: knee osteoarthritis requiring replacement. Father: hypertension; brother: gout.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

ROS: Musculoskeletal: Right knee swelling. No other current joint pain. No generalized myalgia. General: No fever. No chills. No systemic malaise. Neurologic: No distal numbness. No paresthesias. No distal weakness.
model_note.O:
Vitals: BP 138/84 mmHg, P 78 bpm, R 16 rpm, T 98.5 F oral, Pulse Ox 98% on room air, Ht 5' 11", Wt 206 lbs

General: Alert, comfortable at rest.
Musculoskeletal: Small right knee effusion without erythema or deformity. Medial joint-line tenderness and mild warmth; no patellar or fibular-head tenderness. Right knee extends to 0 degrees and flexes to 110 degrees with pain near end flexion; mild crepitus. Knee extension 4+/5 limited by pain; ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion 5/5. Antalgic gait; able to take four steps.
Heart: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+ bilaterally. Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilateral breath sounds.
Osteopathic: L4 right lumbar paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
A: 2. Knee osteoarthritis with an acute flare
P: 1. Protect weight bearing as needed, avoid twisting/squatting and use ice, compression and elevation with safe analgesia. Assess fracture-imaging criteria and ligament stability; consider right knee MRI or orthopedics for persistent catching or true locking. Arrange modified work and review in 1 week. Fever, marked warmth, inability to bear weight or a locked knee warrants urgent reassessment.

2. If chronic symptoms persist, obtain weight-bearing radiographs when indicated and discuss strengthening/physical therapy and activity modification. Explain that degenerative changes may coexist with injury.

3. If crystal or septic arthritis remains possible with increasing warmth/effusion, arrange aspiration for crystals, cell count and culture before assuming gout. Review diuretic and gout management and safe anti-inflammatory options; explain that crystals do not exclude infection, with same-day evaluation for a hot swollen joint or fever.
